instructions: Cut the 1 1/2 lbs beef chuck into 1/2 inch cubes. Pat them dry with paper towels and toss them with 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Finely chop the 2 red onions. Mince the 4 garlic cloves, and peel and mince the ginger until you have about 1 tbsp.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high. Add half the beef in a single layer and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until two sides are deep brown. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and brown the rest of the beef the same way. Transfer it to the plate.

Turn the heat to low. Add 2 tbsp of the ghee and the onions and stir, scraping up the brown bits. Cover and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the onions are very soft and jammy. If they start to stick, add a splash of water. Don't rush the onions. They're what thickens the stew.

Meanwhile, put the 4 eggs in a small pot and cover them with cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn off the heat, cover and leave them for 10 minutes. Transfer them into a bowl of cold water, then peel them and prick each one all over with a fork.
Add the garlic, ginger, 1 tbsp of the ghee and the 1/2 tsp cardamom to the onions. Cook uncovered on low for about 10 minutes, stirring often, until it smells sweet and the garlic is soft.

Stir in 2 tbsp of the berbere and 1 tbsp of the ghee. Cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it turns into a thick, dark red paste. If it catches on the bottom, add a splash of water. Burnt berbere tastes bitter.
Add the beef with its juices, the 3/4 cup broth and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Turn the heat to medium-high and bring it to a boil.

Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until a cube of beef is tender when you press it with a spoon. If it gets thick enough to stick, add a splash of water.
Add the eggs, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes, until they're warmed through.

For anyone who wants more heat, melt the last 1 tbsp ghee in a small pan over low. Stir in the last 1 tbsp berbere for about 30 seconds, until it smells toasty, and transfer it into a small bowl for the table.
Taste the stew. If it's flat, add the last 1/4 tsp salt.
Cut the eggs in half. Serve the stew with the eggs and the injera, with the berbere ghee on the side.
method_notes: Both cook a lot of onion slowly in spiced butter, add garlic, ginger and berbere and cook it into a thick paste, then simmer cubed beef chuck in it until tender and serve it with injera. The Daring Gourmet (the lead) cooks the onions covered on low for a long time, adds the raw beef with broth and simmers about an hour, with optional hard-boiled eggs; Chipa by the Dozen browns the beef first and adds cardamom. This one follows the lead's order and ratios for 4, browns the beef like Chipa does, uses store-bought ghee with cardamom in place of niter kibbeh, and moves a third of the berbere to a hot ghee on the side so the pot is milder. It keeps well for a few days, so it works as a cook-once dinner.
